options: AWS's monitoring service, covering metrics, alarms, logs, and dashboards for most resources automatically
A service that must be manually installed on every EC2 instance before it reports any data
A billing-only tool with no connection to performance data
A replacement for IAM that manages user permissions
questions.explain: CloudWatch is the platform-wide monitoring service that's already watching resources like EC2, S3, and VPC without any setup.

questions.q: Which of these is a default EC2 platform metric, reported with zero setup?
options: CPUUtilization
FreeMemoryBytes
DiskFreeSpacePercent
ApplicationErrorCount
questions.explain: CPUUtilization, along with NetworkIn/Out, DiskReadBytes/WriteBytes, and StatusCheckFailed, come from the hypervisor automatically. Memory and disk-space usage require the CloudWatch Agent.

questions.q: Why doesn't a plain EC2 instance report its free memory the way it reports CPUUtilization?
options: Platform metrics come from the hypervisor watching the instance from outside, and memory usage happens inside the guest OS, which requires an agent to observe
Memory usage is never available anywhere in CloudWatch, even with an agent
AWS considers memory usage a billing metric, not a performance metric
EC2 instances do not have memory
questions.explain: Platform metrics are collected from outside the instance (the hypervisor), so they can't see inside the OS the way an installed agent can.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between basic and detailed EC2 monitoring?
options: Basic monitoring reports every 5 minutes at no extra cost; detailed monitoring reports every 1 minute for a small per-instance charge
Basic monitoring only works for S3, not EC2
Detailed monitoring reports different metrics entirely, not the same data at a different frequency
There is no difference — both terms describe the same feature
questions.explain: The underlying metrics are identical either way; detailed monitoring just increases how often they update, at a small added cost.

questions.q: How do you make CloudWatch track an application-specific value, like orders processed per minute, that AWS doesn't know about by default?
options: Publish it as a custom metric with the PutMetricData API, giving it your own namespace and metric name
Rename one of the existing EC2 platform metrics to match
Custom values can never appear in CloudWatch
Enable detailed monitoring, which automatically creates custom metrics
questions.explain: PutMetricData lets you publish any numeric value under your own namespace, after which it graphs on dashboards exactly like a platform metric.
